title: Finite field and geometric fiber
statement:
Throughout this blueprint, fix a prime $p$ and an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and put $q=p^a$. Set

$$
 k_0=\Fq,
 \qquad
 k=\Fbar\text{ (a fixed algebraic closure of }k_0\text{)},
$$

where $\Fq$ is a field with $q$ elements [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements] and $k$ is an algebraic closure of $k_0$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], with structure homomorphism $\iota:k_0\to k$. The tuple $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ is the *global finite-field datum* used throughout.
For every integer $n\geq1$, let $\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$ be the unique subfield with $q^n$ elements; it exists, is unique, and contains $\iota(k_0)$, so that it is a field extension of $k_0$ [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure]. For any scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], write $|S|$ for its set of closed points [def-weil-closed-points] and, for $s\in|S|$, write $\kappa(s)$ for the residue field at $s$ [def-weil-residue-field]. For a $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, that is, a scheme with a structure morphism $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-affine-spectrum], whose structure morphism is of finite type
[def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write

$$
 Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k,
 \qquad
 a_Y:Y\longrightarrow\Spec k
$$

for its geometric fiber and structure morphism: $Y$ is the base change of $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ along the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ induced by $\iota$ [def-pc-base-change], and $a_Y$ is the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. For every finite-type
$k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ and every $n\geq1$, define

$$
 Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})
 =\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},Y_0\bigr),
 \qquad
 \#Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})=\#\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}
 \bigl(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},Y_0\bigr),
$$

the set of $\mathbf F_{q^n}$-valued points of $Y_0$ over $k_0$ and its number of elements [def-weil-field-valued-points], where $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n}$ is a $k_0$-scheme through the inclusion $k_0\to\mathbf F_{q^n}$ of [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure].
For each prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ for the field of $\ell$-adic numbers and $\Zl$ for its valuation ring, the ring of $\ell$-adic integers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Thus $\Qlb$ is algebraically closed over $\Ql$, and $\Zl$ consists of the
elements of nonnegative $\ell$-adic valuation. A single choice of $\ell$ and
its coefficient fields is understood whenever they occur without a subscript.
For every finite extension $E/\Ql$, write $\mathcal O_E$ for its valuation
ring, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and, for every $n\geq1$, set

$$
 A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,
$$

the finite coefficient ring of $E$ at level $n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against the master blueprint node (order 411) and the slopmaster2 text (01_final_weil_conjectures.tex, def:weil-base-field and def:weil-finite-coefficient-datum, which state the same datum with the transition maps O_E/varpi^{n+1} -> O_E/varpi^n). The text is kept; bracket citations were inserted so that every notion is a statement dependency: the field with q elements, algebraic closure, the unique subfield F_{q^n} of k (stated as a lemma, since existence, uniqueness and the k_0-algebra structure are asserted without argument), schemes, closed points and residue fields (the reviewed nodes def-weil-closed-points and def-weil-residue-field), schemes over a base and Spec, finite type, base change (the existing def-pc-base-change, for Y = Y_0 x_{k_0} k), F_{q^n}-valued points (the reviewed def-weil-field-valued-points), the l-adic numbers and integers, and finite extensions of Q_l with their valuation rings, uniformizers and finite quotients. Of the eight nodes a previous worker left uncommitted for this item, def-weil-scheme-closed-points-residue-field was removed as a duplicate of def-weil-closed-points and def-weil-residue-field; the other seven were checked (statements, sources, Mathlib declarations and line numbers verified in the Mathlib copy) and kept. The finiteness of #Y_0(F_{q^n}) is not asserted here; it is lem-weil-point-counts-finite, which builds on this node.
